chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to find a way to it.' He said, 'He goes out and walks if he does not have [means of transport].' I said, 'He cannot walk.' He said, 'He walks and rides.' I said, 'He cannot do that, meaning walking.' He said, 'He serves the people and goes out with them.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'able to find a way' mean in the context of Hajj obligations?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the gradation of 'istita'ah' (ability) for Hajj, moving from physical capacity to financial means. The Imam establishes that if one lacks the means for travel, serving the caravan (khidmat al-qawm) constitutes sufficient ability, thereby broadening the scope of obligation beyond mere wealth to include service and effort. This interpretation is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the exemption criteria for those with limited resources.
